title: One line of an origin document
$comment: THIS FILE IS AN ORACLE, NOT AN OUTPUT. It says what the bytes are allowed to be, and it is maintained by hand against the protocol rather than against any encoder. When a write fails it, the encoder is wrong, or a human decides deliberately to change this file. Editing it to make a test pass destroys the only thing it is for.
description: A document is a header line followed by one object line per promise, in Dewey id order, joined by newlines. This schema says what ONE line may be. Three rules live above a line and are checked by the reader instead: the first line is the header and there is exactly one, object ids are unique, and object lines are in Dewey order (so o:2 precedes o:10). An unknown line type is legal to READ, because a newer writer may add one, and illegal to WRITE, which is what this schema enforces.

instant.description: Milliseconds since the epoch. Never negative: every deadline derives from a validated timeoutAt or from a clock plus a positive interval.

id.description: A promise id. Everything before the first ':' is the origin, which is the document this line lives in; '.' separates the lineage below it.

address.description: Somewhere a message can be delivered. Any URI with a scheme, deliberately shallow: what follows the scheme belongs to whichever transport is registered for it.

tags.description: Caller-supplied, and load-bearing: resonate:target makes a promise dispatchable, resonate:timer decides whether a deadline resolves or rejects, resonate:scope and resonate:external make it awaitable.

payload.description: A param or a value: headers and data, each omitted when absent. An empty payload is omitted entirely, so if the field is here it says something.

header.description: The first line. Binds the document to the key it lives under and carries what the shell knows that the state machine does not.

v.description: Format version. A const, not a minimum: a new version is a new schema, and a reader that meets a higher one refuses the document rather than guessing.

clk.description: The latest instant observed for this origin. Never decreases. A hint, not state: it is excluded from the comparison that decides whether a write is needed, or every read would be a write.

g.description: Bumped once per committed write. Diagnostic.

og.description: 16 lowercase hex of 64-bit FNV-1a over the origin. A document whose og does not hash the key it was read under is refused rather than answering for another workflow.

ta.description: The one deadline armed for this origin: the earliest of every promise deadline, task retry and task lease below. Omitted when nothing is armed.

tn.description: What the shell called that deadline. Recorded so a writer removes the deadline its own predecessor armed rather than one identified by coordinates that someone else may have re-armed. Present exactly when ta is.

object.description: One promise, and the task that executes it if it has one. They are not two rows that share an id; they are one thing with two faces.

st.description: rejected_timedout is server-owned: no client can name it, and a promise in it was settled by its own deadline.

ca.description: When it was created, or its deadline when it was born past it.

sa.description: When it settled. Omitted while pending.

cb.description: Awaiter ids, in registration order. The order is protocol-visible: a settlement fans out to awaiters in the order they registered. Omitted when empty.

ls.description: Addresses listening for this promise to settle, in registration order. Omitted when empty.

task.description: Present exactly when the promise carries a resonate:target, because a target is what gives a promise somewhere to run.

not.$comment: At most one deadline armed. A task waits to be offered again or waits for its holder to die, never both.

v.description: The fencing token. Every task operation is checked against it, and it rises by exactly one when the task is claimed.

pid.description: The process holding the lease. Present exactly with ttl, and only while acquired.

ttl.description: How long the holder asked to keep the lease. A lease of zero expires at the instant it is granted, so one is the floor.

rs.description: Awaited promises that have settled and that this task has not yet observed. Reported to a worker as a count, not a list. Omitted when empty.

ra.description: When to offer this task again, armed while it is pending and nobody has claimed it.

la.description: When the holder's lease expires, armed while it is acquired.
